summary: Nora Kershaw Chadwick worked in history, archaeology, and other fields, studying at Newnham College (~1911–1915). She later held posts at the University of St Andrews (~1919–1923) and the University of Cambridge (~1950–1958).

Norbert Max Samuelson was a philosopher and religious studies scholar. Educated at Northwestern, Hebrew Union College, and Indiana University under Shlomo Pines, he held positions at Indiana, Brooklyn College, Rutgers, Virginia, Temple (1975–1998), and Arizona State (~1998–2018).

Scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy Noriaki Hakamaya studied at Komazawa University under Shun'ei Hirai and the University of Tokyo under Zuiho Yamaguchi. He served as professor at Komazawa University (1985–2011) and held visiting roles at Wisconsin-Madison.
Noriaki Hosoda is a scholar in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who held positions as assistant (attested 1986) and associate professor (attested 2003) at Hokkaido University.
Noriaki Inoue is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University (~1949–1953) and later served as a professor there (attested 1982).

Buddhist studies scholar Norihiko Tanaka studied at Osaka Kyoiku, Bukkyo, and Visva-Bharati universities. He spent his academic career at Bukkyo University, serving as lecturer (1976), professor (1994, 2013), and professor emeritus (2015–2021).
Norihiko Uchida, working in linguistics and Indology, studied under Yutaka Ochihara and held a post as an assistant at Osaka University of Foreign Studies (attested 1962).

Norihisa Baba is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Hanazono University and the University of Tokyo under Masahiro Shimoda. He joined the University of Tokyo as an assistant in 2006, becoming professor in 2019.
Norio Koyama is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at Shinshu University and under Seitatsu Matsunami. He served as a professor at Taisho University (attested 2014).

Noritoshi Aramaki is a Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology scholar who earned his doctorates at Kyoto University. He served as a professor at Osaka University (~1980–1990), Kyoto University (2000), and Otani University (~2000–2007).

Noriyuki Kudo is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Bukkyo University, where he also lectured (attested 1999–2000). He later served as associate professor at Soka University (attested 2000–2022).

Norman Fischer works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Colgate, Iowa, UC Berkeley, and the Graduate Theological Union, and under Sojun Mel Weitsman and Richard Baker. In 2000, he founded the Everyday Zen Foundation.

Norman Mosley Penzer was an Indology scholar who in 1925 was attested as a member of the Folklore and Royal Asiatic societies, and a fellow of the Royal Anthropological, Royal Geographical, and Geological societies.
Norvin Hein, a scholar of Indology and religious studies, studied under Franklin Edgerton and served as Associate Professor of Comparative Religion in Yale Divinity School (attested 1965).

Buddhist studies scholar Nosei Fuji studied at Dongguk University (1986). He held posts at Daegu University (1988), Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College (attested 2002–2007), and Ryukoku University as Professor of Buddhist Studies (attested 2011–2013).

Notto R. Thelle is a religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies scholar who served as associate director at the NCC Center for the Study of Japanese Religions (1974) and held a post at the University of Oslo (~1986–2011).

Noémie Verdon, an Indologist and historian, completed her PhD at the University of Lausanne (attested 2015) under Johannes Bronkhorst and Charles Genequand, later holding an affiliation at Kyoto University (attested 2018–2019).

Noël Peri, a Japanology and Buddhist studies scholar, taught Western music at Tokyo Music School (1896–1906) and served as resident (1907) and secretary-librarian (1911) at the École Française d'Extrême-Orient.
Nyanabodhi is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies who studied under Ayya Khema as a traditional teacher and later succeeded her.

Buddhist studies scholar Nyanaponika Thera studied at the University of Peradeniya and under Nyanatiloka Mahathera and Mahasi Sayadaw. He founded the Buddhist Publication Society, serving as its director, editor, and president between 1958 and 1988.
